title: compact-KV-scaling-and-hardware-aware-degradation-for-oom-mitigation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Reduce OOM incidents and improve recovery latency by introducing a compact on-GPU KV representation, elastic per-request KV budgets, and a hardware-aware degradation controller that automatically selects graceful fallbacks (quality-preserving compression, short-model cascade, or request-level retry) based on live GPU memory and batch composition telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Decrease GPU OOM rate by >= 70% on the synthetic high-concurrency replay used in incident-2026-01 with identical QPS
End-to-end 95th percentile generation latency increase <= 15% for requests that trigger graceful-degrade compared to baseline (no-OOM baseline), and median latency impact <= 5%
No customer-visible failures for flows marked as 'low-latency-tier' when fallback policy enabled; errors should be converted to degraded-but-successful responses with metadata
E2E integration tests that simulate bursty KV pressure and validate correct selection between compaction, per-request shedding, and model cascade
Runtime flag to force each degradation mode independently for canary verification
Sufficient observability: dashboards with OOM count, degrade-mode breakdown, per-model fallback counts, and token-cost delta per request
technical_notes: Compact-KV: introduce a compacted on-GPU layout that packs KV keys and values with 4-bit-ish descriptor headers and optional per-segment delta-encoding to reduce resident KV size by 2-4x for typical multilingual LLM traces

Elastic per-request KV budget: admission layer sets a per-request 'kv_ticket' derived from request priority, model pinning, and current headroom; tickets can be reserved or stolen by preempt policy for high-priority requests

Hardware-aware degradation controller (HADC): controller consumes GPU telemetry (free bytes, fragmentation score, resident model slices) and batch composition (seq_length histogram). It evaluates policies ordered by least-quality-impact: 1) compact-on-the-fly snap, 2) KV-slimming (trim older prefixes), 3) quantized micro-offload to host for cold KV segments, 4) short-model cascade (e.g., 2-stage decode with condensed model), 5) reject-with-graceful-fallback/retry
Model cascade shim: lightweight adapter routes requests to smaller quantized variant with minimal interface mismatch. Responses include 'fallback_used' metadata for downstream evals
Retry/backoff: jittered exponential retry windows with circuit-breaker that prefers model-cascade + token-shedding over outright fail; backoff respects request idempotency hints provided by API
KB: Modify KV eviction to be prefix-aware and TTL-tagged to avoid evicting recently-used prefixes for high-latency flows (e.g., chat sessions).
Observability: add per-request memory footprint estimation metrics to tracing span; expose 'kv_headroom' and 'frag_score' to Console dashboards
Safety: security_review_required flagged due to new compressed layout metadata being logged to traces; ensure no PII ends up in compacted payloads
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike complete. Implemented prototype compact-KV layout in CUDA kernels (toy model) showing 2.6x resident reduction on our replay trace.
2026-03-02: Integration prototype for elastic kv_ticket integrated into batch admission service; basic policy tests pass locally.

2026-03-08: HADC design reviewed with runtime and infra teams. Feedback: prefer fallback-first policy that favors host-offload over model cascade for multi-tenant nodes. Action: add host-offload threshold and safety window.
2026-03-12: Canary schedule drafted. Will run compact-KV + KV-budget together on 3 dev clusters for 72h prior to limited prod rollout. Need infra approval for canary (ticket INF-1147).
decisions: Adopt on-GPU compact-KV as the primary first-step degradation because it yields the highest memory savings with minimal perf regression.
Make model-cascade the last resort for multi-tenant nodes to avoid noisy neighbor regressions; prefer host-offload when network is healthy.
Expose a per-request 'degradation_policy' header so customers can opt-out of certain fallbacks (e.g., no-model-cascade for high-quality routes).
next_steps: Complete CUDA kernel microbenchmarks and land PR for compact-KV core format
Finish HADC policy engine and wire GPU telemetry into admission-controller
Infra: schedule canary clusters and obtain INF-1147 approval
Create Console panels and add alerts for 'fallback_used' spike > 0.5% of requests
